messages.subject: prediction interval
parts:
Hi Team,

i have a time series model but when I tried to sample from the posterior, I have a IO error. I did check the files and they are there and I am able to run examples in the help file 

formula1 = pos ~ 1 + 
  f(age, model='rw2', constr = F,scale.model=FALSE)+
  f(week_num, model = 'rw2', cyclic = T,constr = F,scale.model=FALSE) +
  f(week, model = 'seasonal', season.length = 52,constr = F,scale.model=FALSE) +
  f(year_week_iid, replicate = age,model='iid')  +
  f(year_week_rw, model='rw2',scale.model=FALSE, replicate = age,constr=F) +
  f(lag_sum, replicate = age, model = "clinear", range = c(0, Inf), constr = F) +
  f(node, model='rw2d', scale.model=FALSE,nrow = nrow, ncol = ncol,constr = F)
 
result1 = inla(formula1, data = covidD, Ntrials = tests,family = "binomial",  control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE, dic = T, cpo = T, waic = T,config = TRUE), verbose = T, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE,link = 1))


post_samples <- inla.posterior.sample(1000, result1, verbose = T)


Error in file(rng.file, "rb") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In system(paste(shQuote(inla.call.no.remote()), "-s -m qsample",  :
  running command '"C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/R/win-library/4.4/INLA/bin/windows/64bit/inla.exe" -s -m qsample -t6:1 -r auto -z 0 -S default -v C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file68601aa04010 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file6860612b7ee8 1 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file686071d24f5 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file686058192b7f C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file68603f8c19e3 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file686047ed7052 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file68606288e9 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file686062246c00 C:/Users/Lennon.Li/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpAthssA/file686024b732a5/file68607aa158d3' had status 1033

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] prediction interval
parts:
I think this says that the computed posterior used for sampling is singular,
hence it fails internally, and does not write any results back, hence trying to
read the file, fails.

can you try to add

diagonal=1e-4

to the rw2, and seasonal models?

also setting

scale.model=TRUE

not FALSE, is generally advisable, to keep things in control (there is a
vignette about why this is the thing to do...)

let me know

best
H

parts:
Cv?   Not with a rolling window.  There is group -cv but not exactly rolling window 
 
 
Best is to use a loop.  You can use the previous fit and restart from there. ( argument control.mode I think’
 
 
Jus keep the dimension of the model the same and do it backwards making more and more data to be NA

—
Haavard Rue

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] prediction interval
parts:
Or use the inla.spde2.pcmatern() model, which is defined for both 2D and 1D; use fmesher::fm_mesh_1d() to define the temporal space. The basic implementation allows alpha=1 and alpha=2 (smoothness like rw1 and rw2, but with matern covariance instead) as well as approximations for fractional orders. For fractional orders, the rSPDE package has better approximations than inla.spde2.pcmatern, for both 1D and 2D.

Finn
